To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- strangeness production is enhanced in heavy ion collisions, - the enhancement is stronger in central than in peripheral collisions, - the effect is stronger for heavier strange hadrons, - it is observed in the S+U, S+S, S+A, S+W, Pb+Pb, Pb+Be and p+Be reactions, - it is not observed in the p+p reactions.
the yields of strange particles are enhanced in central Pb-Pb collisions, while the transverse momentum spectra are similar to those measured in p-Pb and pp reactions.

the production yields and spectra of strange hadrons are enhanced in central Pb-Pb collisions, relative to the yields and spectra in p-Pb and in p-Be collisions, in a way that is qualitatively consistent with the expectations from QGP formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of strange and multi- strange particle production in central Pb-Pb collisions at the SPS energies.
the search for the QCD phase transition to the Quark-Gluon Plasma.
the search for a possible onset of deconfinement and/or the creation of a new phase of matter in Pb-Pb collisions at SPS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data show that strangeness production is enhanced at SPS energies with respect to expectations based on extrapolations from lower energy data and that the enhancement is more pronounced in central Pb-Pb collisions.

the observed strangeness enhancement is a genuine effect, not related to the collision system or to the collision energy, but related to the presence of deconfinement and/or a large hadronic rescattering phase.

there is no evidence for a suppression of strange baryons in Pb-Pb collisions at 40A GeV, and that the production of multi-strange particles is consistent with a thermal model with a chemical freeze-out temperature of Tch ~ 160 MeV, which would imply that strangeness production is in thermal equilibrium with other particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data on strangeness production in central Pb-Pb collisions at SPS energy are compatible with the formation of a QGP.
the data are consistent with a picture of hadronization of a thermalized system of quarks and gluons, the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), in Pb-Pb collisions.
the production of strangeness in central Pb-Pb collisions is consistent with a scenario where the strangeness production is enhanced by the formation of a quark-gluon plasma (QGP).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strangeness enhancement in Pb-Pb collisions at SPS, as compared to p-Pb collisions, can be described by the coalescence model.
strangeness enhancement is a universal feature of high-energy collisions, independent of system size and energy.
the observed yields and spectra are consistent with expectations from a hadron gas, with no evidence for a QGP phase.
